messages.author: 60e43b5243688921
messages.subject: Problem using  specprop()
parts:
Hi all,

i am using the function specprop() in a for loop to analyze several parrot calls. For most calls it works but for some i got this error:

Error in if (any(spec < 0)) stop("Data do not have to be in dB") : 
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

I do not understand why this happens if all the calls were created with the same parameters. 

I would appreciate any help on this.

thanks a lot 

Marcelo Araya-Salas

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Problem using  specprop()
parts:
Hi Marcelo,

This may not be the most helpful answer, but I seem to remember getting
a similar error when I accidentally tried to analyse silence with
spec(). Have you looked at spectrograms of the files that produce the
errors? If you've been filtering or cutting the waves, it's possible
you've cut a odd section that on one particular file results in near
silence, or that the calls are simply to quiet?

This isn't all that likely so I'm not sure if this helps, but it might
give you some place to start for trouble shooting.

Steffi

messages.author: e14cfb57d640984d
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Problem using specprop()
parts:
Hi Marcelo,

Just another idea for troubleshooting... another thing that would be worth trying is looking at the individual calls which give you the error. The specprop() function here is complaining that it's not getting a logical value for the test 

any(spec < 0)

Normally if spec is numeric any() should return either TRUE or FALSE.

So are the spectra which you're passing in valid for the calls which give you the problem?

Best,
Jesse Ross

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Re: setting threshold in timer()
parts:
Hi,

Below is a code I use in a loop to normalize each sound file before using timer function.
Hope it can help
Best Clementine

#load your sound wav file
s<-loadSample(fileName)
#normalize amplitude
s$sound=s$sound/max(abs(s$sound))
#add silence at start to help detection
s<-addsilw(s,at="start",d=0.05,plot=FALSE)
#run timer funtion
times<-timer(s,msmooth=c(200,0),threshold=20,plot=FALSE,f=44100)
